target_customer: Homeowner associations, businesses and city police departments that buy license plate camera subscriptions
problem: Neighborhoods and police lacked affordable, easy to install cameras that capture evidence on vehicles used in property crime.
business_model: Hardware as a service subscription with software, per camera per year
product_category: License plate readers and public safety technology

founders.name: Garrett Langley
founders.background_notes: Media kit says he experienced property crime in his Atlanta neighborhood in 2017. YC page says he recruited two former colleagues.

technical_complexity.rationale: Solar and LTE powered cameras with computer vision plate reading and a cloud search product, mixing hardware and software.

defensibility.rationale: Shared camera network across agencies and installed hardware create stickiness, but readers are an established product category.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents kept selling similar products and did not buy it. Flock grew to over 300M ARR by March 2025.

market_need_then: Founder's own neighborhood property crime was the origin per the media kit. No dated 2017 demand evidence was found.

branding.domain_note: Uses flocksafety.com, legal name Flock Group Inc.

identity.voice_and_tone: Community safety and privacy, 'Better tools for safer communities'

branding.brand_signature: Bird themed product names and a 'spirit bird' employee profile series
branding.community_and_virality: Heavy press and activist attention in 2025 and 2026, including city cancellations, lawsuits and a Senate inquiry, driven by privacy and immigration data sharing concerns.

brand_strength.rationale: Widely known, but 2025 to 2026 coverage is mostly about backlash, with dozens of localities canceling or pausing contracts.

outcome_analysis: Flock grew from a neighborhood camera product into a public safety platform used by many cities, raising 150 million at 3.5 billion in 2022 and 275 million at 7.5 billion in 2025 with over 300 million ARR. The main risk is regulatory and reputational backlash, with dozens of localities canceling or pausing contracts over immigration data sharing, lawsuits and a Senate inquiry.
notes: Series A 2018 (10M, a16z and Kleiner) and Series D 2021 (150M) appear only in aggregators with inconsistent dates and are not recorded. A valuation of 8.3 to 8.4B in April 2026 appears in single aggregator snippets and is unverified. Total raised estimates range from 482M to 1.2B. No competitor source dated near 2017 or 2018 was found; the Vigilant, ELSAG and Axon names come from 2025 and 2026 articles, so the competitor list is left empty. Status is Active; the 2022 round is labeled Series E by some outlets and 2025 round Series F.
